title: Rate and rhythm for the screener

items.question: What is the normal fetal heart rate at a screening scan?
options: 120 to 160 beats per minute, regular
100 to 140 beats per minute, regular
140 to 180 beats per minute, regular
Any rate above 100, regular or not
items.explanation: Normal is 120 to 160 beats per minute with a regular rhythm.

items.question: You see an occasional skipped beat in an otherwise normal heart in a low-risk pregnancy. What does the guideline say about this finding?
options: It is the most common rhythm disturbance, often benign, and usually resolves on its own
It indicates structural heart disease until proven otherwise
It is a sign of fetal hypoxia
It always needs a fetal echocardiogram the same day
items.explanation: Ectopic beats are common, often benign and resolve spontaneously; in low-risk populations they are not associated with increased risk of structural heart disease.

items.question: Every other beat is an ectopic beat, throughout the scan. What next?
options: Arrange further assessment: ectopic beats this frequent are an indication
Reassure; all ectopic beats are benign
Record a normal rhythm
Repeat the scan only if the mother notices reduced movement
items.explanation: Frequent ectopic episodes, more often than every three to five beats, are an indication for further assessment.

items.question: Ectopic beats were first seen three weeks ago. The rhythm has been irregular at every visit since, including today. What next?
options: Arrange further assessment: the rhythm has stayed irregular for more than one to two weeks
Review again in another month
No action; duration does not matter
Stop checking the rhythm at later scans
items.explanation: A rhythm that stays irregular for more than one to two weeks is an indication for further assessment.

items.question: At a second-trimester scan the heart slows for a few seconds while you press to improve the view, then returns to 140. How does the guideline describe this pattern?
options: Transient bradycardia, associated with transducer pressure, which is seen in normal second-trimester fetuses
Atrioventricular block
Persistent bradycardia needing urgent referral
A sign of a structural heart defect
items.explanation: Transient bradycardia associated with transducer pressure is seen in normal second-trimester fetuses. A rate that stays at 110 or below in a well fetus needs timely specialist evaluation.

items.question: The rate stays at 100 beats per minute for the whole examination. The fetus is otherwise well. What next?
options: Timely evaluation by a fetal cardiac specialist
Nothing; this is normal
Recheck at the next routine visit
Record it as probe-pressure bradycardia
items.explanation: Persistent bradycardia at 110 or below in a well fetus needs timely evaluation by a fetal cardiac specialist.

items.question: Which of these is a possible cause of persistent fetal bradycardia?
options: Frequent blocked atrial ectopic beats
Fetal movement
A cardiac axis of 45 degrees
A thin rim of pericardial fluid
items.explanation: Possible causes named in the guideline are frequent blocked atrial ectopic beats, atrioventricular block and sinus bradycardia.

items.question: During active fetal movement the rate rises to 170 beats per minute for a short time and then returns to 150. How is this read?
options: It can be a normal variant
Persistent tachycardia; refer
A tachyarrhythmia
A sign of fetal hypoxia
items.explanation: Mild transient tachycardia of 160 to 180 can be a normal variant during fetal movement.

items.question: The rate stays at 190 beats per minute. What should be considered?
options: A tachyarrhythmia or fetal hypoxia; evaluate further
A normal response to movement
Probe pressure
Nothing, if the four-chamber view is normal
items.explanation: Persistent tachycardia at 180 or more should be evaluated further for tachyarrhythmia or fetal hypoxia.

items.question: Which rhythm finding is listed as an indication for fetal echocardiography?
options: Persistent bradycardia at 110 beats per minute or less
A rate of 150 beats per minute
A single ectopic beat seen once
Brief slowing with probe pressure
items.explanation: Persistent tachycardia (180 or more), suspected heart block or persistent bradycardia (110 or less) and frequent or persistently irregular rhythm are listed fetal indications.

items.question: How does M-mode help the specialist work out the mechanism of an arrhythmia?
options: It times atrial against ventricular contraction with one cursor through an atrial wall and a ventricular free wall
It measures the peak velocity across a valve
It shows the direction of flow in the arches
It measures the size of the heart against the chest
items.explanation: M-mode times atrial against ventricular contraction; the cursor passes through an atrial wall and the free wall of a ventricle together.
